questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to coordinate CronJobs, Jobs, InitContainers, and config-driven rollouts under load with strict security and lifecycle constraints.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job parallelism/completions
- InitContainers for pre-work seeding
- ConfigMap/Secret mounts and config-driven restarts via checksum/config
- SecurityContext controls (runAsNonRoot, capabilities drop)
- Probes for liveness/readiness; TTLAfterFinished

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-processor
  namespace: batch
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      parallelism: 25
      completions: 500
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600
      backoffLimit: 3
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: seed-work
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/files /work/"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: work
                  mountPath: /work
          containers:
            - name: processor
              image: registry.example/image-processor:latest
              volumeMounts:
                - name: config
                  mountPath: /config
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: secrets
                  mountPath: /secrets/api
              readinessProbe: {"httpGet": {"path": "/healthz", "port": 8080}, "initialDelaySeconds": 5, "periodSeconds": 10}
              livenessProbe: {"httpGet": {"path": "/readyz", "port": 8080}, "initialDelaySeconds": 15, "periodSeconds": 20}
              securityContext:
                runAsNonRoot: true
                capabilities:
                  drop: ["ALL"]
          volumes:
            - name: config
              configMap:
                name: files-config
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: secrets
              secret:
                secretName: api-credentials
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          imagePullSecrets:
            - name: regcred
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify 500 tasks complete without SLA breach under load?
- How would you rollback if the ConfigMap change caused incompatibilities?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests secret handling, TLS/mTLS basics, mounting certs, and correct network isolation for a real-world integration.

## Key Concepts
- Secrets and volume mounts
- TLS/Certificates and mTLS basics
- NetworkPolicy egress controls
- Rollout and secret rotation strategies

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: Opaque
data:
  tls.crt: <base64>
  tls.key: <base64>
  ca.crt: <base64>
```

```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payments
        image: payments-api:latest
        env:
        - name: TLS_PATH
          value: /certs
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /certs
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: tls-secret
```

```javascript
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: payments-egress
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.45/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

> Note: DNS-based egress restrictions are not widely supported in NetworkPolicy; use the processor’s IP in the ipBlock.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to choreograph ephemeral canaries using core CKAD primitives: templated Deployment from ConfigMap, secret-based auth, logs via PVC, init containers, probes, and namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy.

## Key Concepts

- ConfigMap templating for Deployment
- Secret-based API tokens and restricted RBAC
- PVC-backed logs and cleanup discipline
- InitContainers for tooling bootstrap
- Readiness/Liveness probes for short-lived canaries
- NetworkPolicy scoped to external dashboard

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-tester
spec:
  schedule: "*/20 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
          containers:
            - name: canary
              image: my-canary-image:latest
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "/canary/run.sh"]
              env:
                - name: DASHBOARD_TOKEN
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: canary-token
                      key: token
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: canary-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rollback a failing canary and propagate the status to the dashboard?
- What are the memory/CPU considerations for rapid-canary spikes and how would you cap them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates understanding of in-cluster automation patterns within CKAD scope: PVC-based manifest storage, ConfigMap-driven templating, InitContainers for tool preparation, Secret management for credentials, TLS sidecars for certificate rotation, and NetworkPolicy for egress control. It tests the ability to design operational solutions that balance functionality with security and maintainability.

## Key Concepts

- **In-cluster manifest application**: Using kubectl directly within pods for declarative resource management
- **Template rendering**: Leveraging ConfigMaps for parameterized manifest generation
- **InitContainers**: Preparing runtime dependencies (kubectl, yq) before main container starts
- **Secret management**: Securely storing API credentials for external service integration
- **TLS certificate rotation**: Sidecar pattern for automatic certificate updates without pod disruption
- **NetworkPolicy**: Namespace-level egress restrictions to limit blast radius
- **RBAC**: ServiceAccount with scoped permissions for least-privilege access
- **Probes**: Readiness and liveness checks for operator reliability

## Evaluation Criteria

Strong candidates will address:
1. Proper RBAC scoping to namespace-level permissions
2. Idempotent manifest application using `kubectl apply`
3. Security considerations around elevated pod privileges
4. Trade-offs between simplicity and operational overhead
5. Handling of template rendering and variable substitution

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical CKAD skills: PVC-backed logs, ConfigMap-driven behavior, Secrets, InitContainers, sidecars for TLS rotation, health checks, and namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy, all in a minimal Deployment.

## Key Concepts

- PVC-backed log ingestion
- ConfigMap-driven batching (BATCH_SIZE)
- InitContainer for bootstrap deps
- Secret for credentials
- TLS rotation sidecar pattern
- Readiness and liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for restricted egress

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: log-forwarder
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: log-pvc
        - name: tls
          secret:
            secretName: log-tls
      initContainers:
        - name: init-deps
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tls
              mountPath: /tls
      containers:
        - name: forwarder
          image: your-registry/log-forwarder:latest
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tls
              mountPath: /tls
          env:
            - name: DEST_URL
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: log-config
                  key: DEST_URL
            - name: BATCH_SIZE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: log-config
                  key: BATCH_SIZE
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: log-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      serviceAccountName: log-sa
      restartPolicy: Always
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test TLS rotation in CI?
- How would you scale this pattern across many namespaces while preserving isolation?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to combine CronJobs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and NetworkPolicy to automate in-namespace validation and remediation with idempotent patching and durable logs.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob, InitContainer, ConfigMap, Secret
- In-cluster scripting with kubectl/jq
- API-driven remediation and PVC-based logs
- Namespace NetworkPolicy RBAC considerations

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton (CronJob with remediation Job)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-test-runner
spec:
  schedule: '0 * * * *'
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubectl jq"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          containers:
            - name: runner
              image: bitnami/kubectl:1.28
              command: ["sh", "-c", "bash /scripts/run.sh"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
                - name: policy
                  mountPath: /policy
                - name: secret
                  mountPath: /secret
              readinessProbe:
                httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: ns-logs-pvc
            - name: policy
              configMap:
                name: ns-test-policy
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to constrain scheduling to hardware and perform safe rolling updates for GPU workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NodeSelector and taints/tolerations
- GPU resource requests/limits
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RollingUpdate strategy and preStop
- Verification and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ai-processor
  namespace: ml
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ai-processor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ai-processor
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        hardware: gpu
      tolerations:
      - key: hardware
        operator: Equal
        value: gpu
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: ai-processor
        image: your-image:tag
        resources:
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "500m"
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "4Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /live
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 1
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Deploy and verify pods schedule on GPU nodes: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide`
2. Check GPU allocation: `kubectl describe nodes | grep nvidia.com/gpu`
3. Load test with concurrent requests while monitoring pod health
4. Verify rolling updates maintain availability: `kubectl rollout status deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
5. Monitor GPU utilization during load: `nvidia-smi` on target nodes

## Rollback Strategy
1. Use deployment revision history: `kubectl rollout history deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
2. Quick rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
3. For critical issues, scale to zero then redeploy previous stable version
4. Monitor rollback progress and verify pod health and GPU allocation

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical batch-job composition: init tooling, config-driven scripts, and safe cleanup. 

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Job TTL, backoff, and completion semantics
- InitContainers alongside main containers
- ConfigMap and Secret mounts; env from Secret
- Resource requests/limits; idempotence

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
  namespace: migrate
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
  backoffLimit: 3
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client"]
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: postgres:15
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
          env:
            - name: PGHOST
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: host
          command: ["psql","-h","$(PGHOST)","-U","$(POSTGRES_USER)","-d","migration_db","-f","/migrate/scripts/migrate.sql"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: migrate-scripts
              mountPath: /migrate/scripts
      volumes:
        - name: migrate-scripts
          configMap:
            name: migrate-scripts
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate idempotence for repeated runs?
- How would you rollback if migration fails after partial progress?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD fundamentals: per-namespace automation, ConfigMaps/Secrets usage, PVC-backed data, InitContainer provisioning, and health checks with NetworkPolicy. It focuses on real data-retention workflows and safe auditing.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace CronJob and Job orchestration
- ConfigMap and Secret consumption in pods
- PVC-mounted data processing and log handling
- InitContainer provisioning and readiness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for controlled egress

## Code Example

```yaml
# minimal skeleton for the CronJob (CKAD-style)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-retention-purge
  namespace: default
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-utils
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache coreutils curl jq"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          containers:
            - name: purge
              image: alpine:3.18
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: retention-config
              env:
                - name: API_KEY
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: purge-secret
                      key: api-key
              command: ["sh", "-c", "set -e; /bin/sh -c 'find ${TARGET_PATH} -type f -mtime +${RETENTION_DAYS} -print0 | xargs -0 rm -f' || true; curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"namespace":"$(POD_NAMESPACE)","ts":"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}' https://audit.example.internal/api/v1/purge -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' || true"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: logs-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          serviceAccountName: pod-sa
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotency and ensure no data loss during concurrent purges?
- How would you scale this with thousands of namespaces without overwhelming the audit endpoint?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical drift detection in multiple namespaces, using PVCs, InitContainers and in-cluster API calls.

## Key Concepts

- In cluster tooling with InitContainers, Secrets, and PVCs
- Drift vs validation and how to compare live state
- Namespace scoped RBAC and NetworkPolicy
- Tooling: kubeval, kubectl, client-go in a container

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: drift-detector
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: drift-manifests
      - name: drift
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: drift-reports
      initContainers:
      - name: setup-tools
        image: alpine:3.17
        command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl kubectl kubeval"]
      containers:
      - name: detector
        image: drift-detector:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
        - name: drift
          mountPath: /drift
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /ready
          port: 8080
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
```

- How would you secure credentials and rotate secrets?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical resource governance: ephemeral storage limits, per-pod boundaries, and maintenance reliability via PodDisruptionBudget. It mirrors real-world ops constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Ephemeral storage limits and LimitRange
- Per-pod resource requests/limits
- PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable
- Patch-and-rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# LimitRange example
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: quota-demo-limits
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      ephemeral-storage: "2Gi"
    min:
      ephemeral-storage: "200Mi"
    default:
      ephemeral-storage: "1Gi"
    defaultRequest:
      ephemeral-storage: "1Gi"
    type: Container
```
```yaml
# Deployment patch (snippet)
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: worker
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
            ephemeral-storage: "1Gi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
            ephemeral-storage: "2Gi"
```
```yaml
# PodDisruptionBudget
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: worker-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: worker
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adjust if a node lacks enough ephemeral storage to honor the limit? 
- How would you test the patch in a staged environment before production rollback?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical patching skills for CKAD: config, secrets, scheduling, and lifecycle under disruption.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap mounting and envFrom
- topologySpreadConstraints distribution
- PodDisruptionBudget semantics
- Resource requests/limits and QoS
- Probes and preStop lifecycle
- Rollback verification via rollout status

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: worker
  namespace: queue
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: worker-config
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: your-image
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/worker/config
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: worker-credentials
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 80
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 5"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "256Mi"
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll back if the patch caused issues?
- How would you validate topology spread in a multi-zone environment?
